productTitle: Vintage Western Bolo Tie — braided leather cord, cast-metal slide (cowboy hat / longhorn / concho / Texas star / eagle / bison motifs)

scenes.prompt: Commissioned still-life for Garden & Gun, shot by Squire Fox on a Hasselblad H6D-100c, HC 80mm at f/5.6. On a stitched saddle-leather valet tray atop a reclaimed-walnut ranch dresser, the bolo tie rests coiled — cast-metal slide face-up, braided black-leather cord in one relaxed loop, both engraved aglet tips fanned slightly apart. Render the product EXACTLY as the reference image: same slide motif, antique metal finish, cord and tips, nothing redesigned. Low three-quarter about 25 degrees above the surface, warm late-afternoon light raking from the left. Homey color-echo: the metal finish repeats in an aged-brass drawer pull and a worn brass key; the black cord grounds crisp against honey-toned walnut. Two or three lived-in props only — a folded oat-linen cloth, one dried sage sprig, a worn leather watch strap. Concrete imperfections: a thumb-tarnish smudge on the slide edge, a knot-crease in the cord, a pale ring-mark on the walnut, dust film in the raking light. Single bolo tie, no people, no hands, no neck, no alcohol, no Chinese text, no captions. Portra-400 grain in shadow mids, 2 percent vignette, true-dark corners, color cast kept warm and surface-local.

Documentary editorial for Cowboys & Indians, photographed Davidson-style on a Hasselblad H6D-100c, HC 50mm at f/5.6. A worn charcoal-felt western hat lies crown-down on weathered cedar planks; the bolo tie drapes across the upturned brim, slide resting in the felt with the braided cord trailing over the brim edge and the two metal tips dangling free. Reproduce the bolo EXACTLY as the reference — same slide design, antique finish, cord and aglet tips, unchanged. Eye-to-chest-level slight three-quarter, soft diffused mid-morning daylight from a window out of frame, no ring-flash blowouts on the metal. Southwestern palette: roughly 75 percent warm earth (felt charcoal warmed by cedar, tan hatband, saddle leather), a cream linen accent, one restrained cool note. Two props only: a coil of waxed twine and one stem of dried wheat. Concrete flaws: a sweat-darkened ridge on the felt brim, a 1 millimeter scratch on one aglet, split grain in the cedar, a lint fibre on the felt beside the slide. Single bolo tie only, no people, no hands, no neck or body, no alcohol, no signage or text. Shallow depth of field, the cord falling to bokeh, faint grain, corners true-dark.

Refined still-life in the WSJ Magazine register, shot on a Hasselblad H6D-100c, HC 120mm macro at f/5.6. A single floating shelf of deep clay-painted oak against a moody forest-green plaster wall; the bolo tie hangs vertically from a small forged-iron peg at the shelf's edge, slide centered, braided cord dropping straight, the two engraved tips at rest. Render the bolo EXACTLY as the reference — identical slide motif, antique metal finish, cord, and tips. Tight 30 percent framing, near-empty negative space, one controlled shaft of cool late-afternoon light grazing the slide so casting texture and bezel read sharp. Gallery-minimal: the green wall and clay shelf carry the color while the antique metal stays the brightest, most-resolved thing in frame. No props beyond the iron peg. Concrete imperfections: a hairline casting seam on the slide, a thumb-burnished worn high spot, a chip in the clay paint at the shelf corner, fine dust on the upper edge. Single bolo tie, no people, no hands, no neck, no alcohol, no text or watermark. One exposure, corners true-dark, the brightest metal specular just clipping, Portra-400 grain in shadows, 1 to 2 percent vignette, zero global color cast.

Wallpaper*-style overhead knoll, photographed on a Hasselblad H6D-100c with an HC 120mm macro at f/8. Direct 90-degree top-down view onto a sun-bleached raw-oak board with visible tool marks; the bolo tie is laid as the anchor — slide flat at center, the braided black-leather cord arranged in a loose asymmetric S into clean negative space, the two metal tips fanned a few centimeters apart. Reproduce the bolo EXACTLY as the reference: same slide design, antique finish, cord and tips. Crisp graphic composition, soft even midday daylight, a short soft-edged contact shadow beneath the slide so it sits on the wood rather than floating. Minimalist palette: pale oak and black cord only, one small cool note from a strip of selvedge denim laid along the board's lower edge. Concrete flaws: a knot-crease where the cord was bent, casting strike marks on the slide face, a dust speck beside (not on) the slide, a split in the oak grain. Single bolo tie only, no people, no hands, no neck or body, no alcohol, no captions, no Chinese characters. Real depth-of-field falloff at the cord ends, faint Portra grain in shadow mids, 1 percent vignette, color staying neutral and surface-local.

Editorial for T: The New York Times Style Magazine, shot Sturman-style on a Hasselblad H6D-100c, HC 80mm at f/5.6. The bolo tie hangs as-worn from an aged forged-iron wall hook on a warm limewashed adobe-toned wall; the slide drops at chest height, braided cord falling in a natural vertical loop, engraved tips swinging just apart. Render the bolo EXACTLY as the reference — same motif, antique metal finish, cord and aglet tips, unchanged. Eye-level straight-on with a slight three-quarter lean, warm golden-hour side light from a window out of frame casting a soft long shadow on the wall. Color-echo homey: the iron hook and a small framed tintype echo the metal finish; the warm wall grounds the black cord. Restrained props — only the hook and one trailing dried sagebrush stem. Concrete imperfections: rust bleeding through the hook's worn paint, a knot-crease in the cord, a faint tarnish smudge on the slide, a hairline crack in the limewash. Single bolo tie, no people, no hands, no neck, no alcohol, no signage or text. Shallow depth of field, the lower cord softening to bokeh, faint grain, 2 percent vignette, corners true-dark, warm light kept local.

Quiet Kinfolk-style field-notes still-life on a Hasselblad H6D-100c, HC 120mm macro at f/5.6. On a cool slate slab, a folded length of selvedge denim and a band of raw oat-linen form the ground; the bolo tie rests coiled on the linen edge, slide face-up and lifted slightly on the fabric fold so it casts a short contact shadow, cord in a relaxed coil, tips resting together. Reproduce the bolo EXACTLY as the reference: same slide design, antique finish, cord, and tips. Low three-quarter at about 20 degrees, soft cool morning light from the left, no blowouts on the metal. Minimalist cool palette: slate grey, indigo denim, oat linen, the antique metal the single bright focal pop. One prop only — a small raw turquoise chunk set deliberately to the side. Concrete flaws: a frayed selvedge thread, a thumb-tarnish on the slide edge, dust film on the slate in raking light, a lint fibre on the linen. Single bolo tie, no people, no hands, no neck, no alcohol, no text or watermark. Shallow depth of field with cord ends to bokeh, Portra-400 grain in shadow mids, 1 to 2 percent vignette, neutral surface-local color, corners true-dark.

Mandatory extreme macro for a Wallpaper* materials feature, shot on a Hasselblad H6D-100c, HC 120mm macro at f/4, 1:1 to 2:1 magnification. Frame fills with the cast-metal slide face and one engraved aglet tip, the braided black-leather cord curving in from the slide and falling immediately to soft bokeh. Reproduce the slide and tip EXACTLY as the reference — same motif, antique metal finish, casting and engraving, nothing altered. Render the hand-tooling and casting texture, the relief of the motif, the bezel edges, the aglet crimp and its fine engraving razor-sharp; the braided cord weave crisp where it meets the slide, then dissolving. A controlled soft reflection on the polished high points hints at a warm window, not a mirror, not a void. Single deliberate light from upper left, cool-neutral fill, no ring-flash. Macro-scale imperfections: a 1 to 2 millimeter scratch across the slide face, thumb-tarnish darkening one engraved groove, a casting strike mark, a dust mote on the cord weave. Single bolo tie detail only, no people, no hands, no neck, no alcohol, no text or watermark. Extreme shallow depth of field, true macro falloff, faint Portra grain in shadow mids, corners true-dark.
